content.overview: Section 223 requires an inspector appointed under the Chapter to make an interim report to the Central Government if so directed, and a final report on the conclusion of the investigation. The Central Government may forward a copy of the report to the company and to any person whose conduct is dealt with, and may cause the report to be published. A copy of the report authenticated in the manner the section provides may be admissible in legal proceedings as evidence of the opinion of the inspector in relation to any matter contained in the report.
content.glance: Inspector: interim report if directed; final report to CG on conclusion; CG may forward to company/persons dealt with and may publish; authenticated copy admissible as evidence of inspector’s opinion.
content.study: An inspector appointed under this Chapter shall, if so directed by the Central Government, make interim reports to that Government, and on the conclusion of the investigation shall make a final report to the Central Government. Every report shall be written or printed as directed. The Central Government may forward a copy of any report to the company and to any person dealt with, and may cause the report to be published. A copy of any report of any inspector or inspectors authenticated in the manner provided may be admissible in any legal proceeding as evidence of the opinion of the inspector in relation to any matter contained in the report. Current-law framing: confirm appointment and direction for interim report if any; final report on conclusion; CG’s powers to forward and publish; evidentiary use of authenticated copy as opinion evidence subject to the section.

sections.heading: Reports
sections.body: Interim report if directed by CG; final report on conclusion of investigation; written or printed as directed.

sections.heading: Forwarding and Publication
sections.body: CG may forward a copy to the company and to persons whose conduct is dealt with; may cause the report to be published.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Use
sections.body: Authenticated copy may be admissible in legal proceedings as evidence of the inspector’s opinion on matters in the report.

examples.title: Final report and publication
examples.body: On conclusion of a s. 210 investigation the inspector submits a final report to the Central Government. CG may forward it to the company and cause it to be published under s. 223.

examples.title: Opinion evidence
examples.body: In a later prosecution an authenticated copy of the inspector’s report is tendered. Under s. 223 it may be admissible as evidence of the inspector’s opinion on matters contained in the report, subject to the section’s conditions.

hypotheticals.question: Is the inspector’s report under s. 223 itself a conviction?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The report is submitted to the Central Government. It may be used as evidence of the inspector’s opinion and may form the basis for action under s. 224, but it is not itself an adjudication of guilt.

distinctions.title: Inspector’s report (s. 223) vs report on inspection (s. 208)
distinctions.left: Report after formal investigation by appointed inspector
distinctions.right: Report after Registrar/inspector inspection or inquiry under s. 206

misconceptions.trap: The inspector’s report is automatically binding as a court judgment.
misconceptions.correction: The report goes to the Central Government. An authenticated copy may be admissible as evidence of the inspector’s opinion; action on the report is under s. 224. It is not a court judgment.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 223 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm inspector appointment and report stage. II. Note interim/final duties. III. CG forwarding/publication. IV. Evidentiary use. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Report status; forwarding; evidentiary issues; precise relief.

examTips: Interim if directed; final on conclusion.
